extracted.intended_audience: potential consortium applicants, voice service providers, and participants in the FCC rulemaking (Docket No. EB 20-22)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for (1) entities seeking registration as the single private-led traceback consortium under the TRACED Act and (2) parties filing comments, ex parte presentations, and IRFA/PRA responses in the FCC rulemaking (EB 20-22). Covers required certifications, application content, procedural filing rules, and suggested content/format for comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consortium identification standard
rubrics_metrics.description: By what standard should the consortium identify voice service providers that are originating unlawful robocall campaigns, and how should the consortium assess whether a campaign is 'large-scale'?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Further Notice asks commenters to define: what 'unlawful robocall campaign' means; whether 'unlawful robocall' is narrower than 'suspected unlawful robocall' and what level of certainty is required; when a series of unlawful calls becomes a 'campaign' (e.g., coordinated pattern); and whether 'large-scale' should be defined by call volume alone or include other factors such as burden on networks. Commenters should propose measurable/operational standards for identification and scale assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition / certainty level for 'unlawful robocall'
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the term 'unlawful robocall' in section 4(b)(5)(C) narrower than 'suspected unlawful robocall' in section 13, and if so, what level of certainty does it require?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission requests input on the appropriate evidentiary or confidence threshold the consortium should use to classify calls as 'unlawful' versus 'suspected unlawful' (e.g., reasonable belief, preponderance, documented evidence). Commenters should explain tradeoffs between false positives/negatives and timeliness of action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for when calls constitute a 'campaign'
rubrics_metrics.description: At what point would a series of unlawful calls become a 'campaign'?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether 'campaign' implies coordination or pattern, thresholds for number/ rate/temporal clustering of calls, origin concentration, or other indicia of coordinated activity. Provide concrete metrics or algorithms where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of 'large-scale' campaigns
rubrics_metrics.description: How should the consortium assess whether a campaign is 'large-scale'?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss whether 'large-scale' should be measured by absolute call volume, percentage of traffic, geographic spread, network impact, or combined factors. Address network burden and operational impacts in addition to raw counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Actions required of identified providers
rubrics_metrics.description: Once a provider has been identified by the registered consortium, the Commission must require such a provider to take action to ensure that such provider does not continue to originate such calls and to make reasonable efforts to minimize the burden of any robocall mitigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Further Notice solicits suggestions on specific actions: prescribe mitigation practices; require close monitoring; require compliance plans and periodic reports; require point-of-contact responsiveness; implement know-your-customer (KYC) obligations; and implement internal traffic monitoring and response to aberrant patterns. Commenters should evaluate benefits and drawbacks and propose concrete, minimally burdensome approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prescribed robocall mitigation practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Should the Commission prescribe specific robocall mitigation practices for providers that repeatedly originate large-scale unlawful robocall campaigns, and if so, what practices?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include sinkholing, traffic rate-limiting, enhanced onboarding/KYC, additional authentication checks, or routing controls. Commenters should specify the practice, when it applies, operational steps, and expected burdens and benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Close monitoring and who performs it
rubrics_metrics.description: Should we require an identified provider to submit to close monitoring of its practices? Should the Commission, the registered consortium, or an independent third party monitor these practices?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss scope/frequency of monitoring, who is the appropriate monitor (self-monitoring with reports, consortium audits, independent third-party audits), confidentiality protections, and mechanisms to minimize burdens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance plans and periodic reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Should we require an identified provider to submit a compliance plan and periodic reports on its efforts to conform to that plan?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If yes, specify expected elements of the plan (mitigation steps, timelines, metrics), reporting cadence (e.g., monthly/quarterly), required supporting data, and procedures for Commission review. Address confidentiality and burden considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Point-of-contact and response time
rubrics_metrics.description: Should we propose that an identified provider make a point of contact available to the Commission, the consortium, and others and to respond to concerns within a specified period of time, such as 14 days?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider recommending acceptable response windows, duties of the contact, escalation procedures, and how contact information is provided/updated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Know-your-customer (KYC) obligations and reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Should we require an identified provider to implement know-your-customer obligations—and report the contact information for each of its customers to the registered consortium or the Commission?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe what KYC entails (identity verification, documentation), thresholds for which customers require KYC, data fields to report, privacy/confidentiality safeguards, and burdens on providers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal traffic monitoring and aberrant-pattern response
rubrics_metrics.description: Should we require identified providers to implement internal measures to monitor the traffic transiting their networks to ensure that it is consistent with legitimate voice traffic and to act in response to aberrant patterns?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide examples of monitoring measures (statistical anomaly detection, fingerprinting known bad patterns), thresholds for action, automated vs. manual responses, and reporting/recordkeeping expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimizing burdens of mitigation
rubrics_metrics.description: How can we ensure that any robocall mitigation requirements are not overly burdensome, but achieve the goal of mitigating robocalls originated by providers identified as originating large-scale unlawful robocall campaigns?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weigh mitigation efficacy against compliance costs. Propose tailored, risk-based obligations, phased implementation, safe harbors for good-faith implementers, and ways to limit impacts on legitimate traffic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Openness / neutrality in consortium participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Our openness principle for demonstrating neutrality focuses on allowing voice service providers to participate but does not exclude a consortium from addressing concerns about call blocking; consortium must demonstrate neutrality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consortium applications should explain policies that preserve neutrality (avoid conflicts of interest, participation rules, governance transparency) and how they will prevent improper call blocking or bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual public notice and filing deadline (April 28)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Enforcement Bureau shall issue a public notice no later than April 28 annually seeking registration of a single consortium that conducts private-led efforts to trace back the origin of suspected unlawful robocalls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must file in response to the annual public notice by the date specified in that notice. The current registered consortium continues until the effective date of any new selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consortium registration: neutral third-party demonstration
rubrics_metrics.description: An entity that seeks to register must 'Demonstrate that the consortium is a neutral third party competent to manage the private-led effort to trace back the origin of suspected unlawful robocalls.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide organizational structure, governance, conflict-of-interest policies, technical competence, staff qualifications, and examples of prior traceback or related operations to substantiate neutrality and competence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consortium registration: written best practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a copy of the consortium’s written best practices, with an explanation thereof, regarding the management of its traceback efforts and regarding voice service providers’ participation in the consortium’s efforts to trace back the origin of suspected unlawful robocalls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit the full best-practices document and an explanatory statement describing how practices will be applied, updated, and enforced. Include safeguards against misuse of data and measures to reduce false positives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consortium certification of focus on fraudulent/abusive/unlawful traffic
rubrics_metrics.description: Certify that, consistent with section 222(d)(2) of the Communications Act, the consortium’s efforts will focus on fraudulent, abusive, or unlawful traffic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a binding certification and explain operational criteria and controls that ensure traceback is targeted to those categories of traffic only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advance notice to Commission of traceback intent
rubrics_metrics.description: Certify that the consortium has notified the Commission that it intends to conduct traceback efforts of suspected unlawful robocalls in advance of registration as the single consortium.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include documentation or evidence of prior notification to the Commission and provide proposed communication protocols for future notifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consortium commitments if selected (ongoing compliance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Certify that, if selected to be the registered consortium, it will remain in compliance with the requirements, conduct an annual review to ensure compliance, and promptly notify the Commission of any changes that reasonably bear on its certification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should pledge procedures for annual compliance reviews, mechanisms for internal audit, and a process/timeline for notifying the Commission of material changes. Describe what changes would be reported and how.

rubrics_metrics.name: No re-filing requirement for registered consortium
rubrics_metrics.description: The entity selected to be the registered consortium will not be required to file the letter mandated in paragraph (b) in subsequent years after the consortium’s initial registration; initial certifications continue for the duration of each subsequent year unless notified otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registered consortiums should maintain current certifications and notify the Commission in writing on or before the filing date in the annual public notice if they intend to change or withdraw certifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuity of traceback efforts
rubrics_metrics.description: The current registered consortium shall continue its traceback efforts until the effective date of the selection of any new registered consortium.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure operational continuity during any transition; prospective applicants and the Commission should consider handover procedures and timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment filing: method and copies
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments may be filed using the Commission’s Electronic Comment Filing System (ECFS). Paper filers must file an original and one copy of each filing; if multiple docket numbers appear, filers must submit two additional copies for each additional docket or rulemaking number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Electronic Filers: use ECFS (http://apps.fcc.gov/ecfs/). Paper Filers: send by hand/messenger, commercial overnight courier, or first-class/overnight USPS to the Commission Secretary; addresses and special delivery instructions appear in the document (e.g., hand deliveries to 445 12th St., SW, Room TW-A325 when HQ is open). Follow filing hours and envelope procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment filing: substantive content and formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments must include a short and concise summary of the substantive arguments raised and must comply with section 1.49 of the Commission’s rules and all other applicable sections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct all parties to include the name of the filing party and the date of the filing on each page. All parties are encouraged to use a table of contents and are strongly encouraged to track the organization set forth in the Further Notice to facilitate internal review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ex parte presentations: permit-but-disclose rules and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: This proceeding is a 'permit-but-disclose' proceeding. Persons making ex parte presentations must file a copy of any written presentation or a memorandum summarizing any oral presentation within two business days after the presentation (unless a different deadline for the Sunshine period applies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Memoranda summarizing oral presentations must (1) list all persons attending or otherwise participating in the meeting and (2) summarize all data presented and arguments made. If the presentation reflected data/arguments already in the presenter’s written filings, the presenter may provide citations to those filings (specifying page/paragraph numbers) instead of summarizing them. Documents shown or given to Commission staff during ex parte meetings are deemed written ex parte presentations and must be filed consistent with section 1.1206(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ex parte filing formats and native file requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Written ex parte presentations and memoranda summarizing oral ex parte presentations, and all attachments thereto, must be filed through the electronic comment filing system in proceedings with electronic filing available, and must be filed in their native format (e.g., .doc, .xml, .ppt, searchable.pdf).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare submissions in native, machine-searchable formats to comply; include attachments and supporting data in original file formats where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: IRFA responses and designation
rubrics_metrics.description: Written public comments are requested on the Initial Regulatory Flexibility Analysis (IRFA); comments must be filed by the deadlines for comments on the Further Notice and must have a separate and distinct heading designating them as responses to the IRFA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When filing comments that address the IRFA, include a clearly labeled section heading (e.g., 'Response to IRFA') and respond to the IRFA questions. These IRFA responses should be timely and filed per the docket deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paperwork Reduction Act (PRA) comment invitation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Further Notice contains proposed new information collection requirements. The Commission invites the general public and OMB to comment on the information collection requirements contained in this document, as required by the PRA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide estimates of burden hours, affected respondents, and ways to minimize paperwork burdens. Pursuant to the Small Business Paperwork Relief Act, the Commission also seeks comment on how to reduce information collection burden for small business concerns with fewer than 25 employees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility for people with disabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: To request material in accessible formats for people with disabilities (braille, large print, electronic files, audio format), contact fcc504@fcc.gov or call the Consumer & Governmental Affairs Bureau at the provided voice/tty numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the specified contact methods for requests and ensure timely fulfillment of accessible-format requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date of rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The rules adopted in the Report and Order and Further Notice shall be effective 30 days after publication in the Federal Register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan implementation timelines and compliance activities with the 30-day post-publication effective date in mind.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment organization recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties are encouraged to use a table of contents and to track the organization set forth in the Further Notice to facilitate the Commission’s internal review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure comments to mirror the Notice’s questions and headings to make it easier for reviewers to locate responses to specific issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing identification on each page
rubrics_metrics.description: Include the name of the filing party and the date of the filing on each page of comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This aids processing and record integrity. Ensure consistent header/footer usage across all pages and attachments.
